marks.why: 4.9s is long for one question; 13 words means 5-6 caption flips before the payoff. The frozen hand is a good start, but the line is abstract with sound off.
marks.fix_line: Pay with a coin nobody can read? What's in it?
marks.fix_picture: Open mid-action: the coin is already hitting the palm at 0.0s. Burn a big '?' over the pale coin by 1.0s.

marks.why: 'Make it pure gold' answers the hook at 5s. The curiosity gap closes and lines 4-10 have to rebuild it.
marks.fix_picture: Keep the Met stater slam, full-frame, with a hard cut and a hit sound.

marks.why: Museum-label dump (earliest known, 8 g, Sardis) on a slow zoom right after the reveal. Nothing is at stake and nothing moves. This is the biggest swipe point.
marks.fix_line: One of the earliest known. Found at Sardis.
marks.fix_picture: Replace the slow zoom with two fast push-ins (lion, then bull), 1.5s each. Drop the '8 g' tag or flash it for 0.5s at most.

marks.why: Jumps back to the problem after the answer. A frowning trader is weak and doesn't show 'half silver' without sound.
marks.fix_line: Before it? A coin might be half silver.
marks.fix_picture: The pale coin splits on screen: the left half gold, the right half grey. Caption 'HALF SILVER?'

marks.why: Two quick questions; the streak changing colour on the stone is a concrete visual.
Fast process montage (salt, bake, crack, glint) with short lines and a change of picture every 1-2s. This is the strongest stretch.
'Now prove it' re-hooks well before the last act.
'Pure silver' is confusing: silver was just the impurity being removed. A cold viewer stumbles here.
marks.fix_line: Stamp a lion and bull. Pure gold, or pure silver.
marks.fix_picture: Split-screen the two strikes side by side, labelled GOLD and SILVER, so the two coin types read as separate.

marks.why: A short credit beat with a bow gag.
'Before that...' plus the matched frame 1 makes a clean loop into the hook.

line_edits.text: One of the earliest known. Found at Sardis.
Stamp a lion and bull. Pure gold, or pure silver.
